Interpretability experiments on
language models. The recurring move: write down the simplest possible
mathematical model of some LLM behaviour, then test it with carefully designed experiments.
The simple models might be wrong in interesting ways — and the wrongness
is what teaches you something about what the model is actually doing.

Everything here reproduces on a laptop. The models I use are GPT-2
small (124M) and the smaller Pythia variants (70M, 160M), chosen so
experiments run in minutes, not hours.
